title: Over a decade since Yolanda, thousands of housing units remain empty
summary: MANILA, Philippines — Thousands of homes built for survivors of Super Typhoon Yolanda (Haiyan) remain unoccupied more than a decade after the storm devastated the Visayas, unleashing storm surges…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Thousands of homes built for survivors of Super Typhoon Yolanda (Haiyan) remain unoccupied more than a decade after the storm devastated the Visayas, unleashing storm surges reaching about two meters high. Through the National Housing Authority’s (NHA) Yolanda Permanent Housing Program, the government had a revised target of 194,195 units. As of December 2025, only 176,804, or 91.04 percent have been completed so far. Out of this, 47,139 units remain vacant, according to the Commission on Audit’s (COA) 2025 Consolidated Report on the Audit of Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Funds released in August 2026.
